topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and states what students should learn about cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations accumulate and confer selective advantages within the biological conditions that permit cancer to develop.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and the evidence for their contribution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk despite uncertainty and variation in who develops cancer.

topics.label: Infectious agents as causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive carcinogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example.

topics.label: Mechanisms of carcinogen-induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage that can become mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutational initiation from the promotional conditions that allow initiated cells to proliferate into tumours.

topics.label: Tissue and life-stage susceptibility, with a recap of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: The discussion of context-dependent susceptibility concludes the account of carcinogen mechanisms, which the following subtopic recaps.

topics.label: Methods for investigating carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence of carcinogenicity is obtained and the limitations of the methods used.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture’s conclusions about environmental cancer risks and carcinogen assessment through the framing of everyday risk–benefit decisions.
